lines.text: Why do you lurch forward when a bus suddenly brakes?
lines.visual: Local bus drives across a Mumbai-style street. Mascot Newt (little robot student) stands inside holding a pole. Bus screeches, Newt squashes and stretches forward. Freeze-frame with a big question mark.

lines.text: Nobody pushed you. So what just happened?
lines.visual: Rewind effect, slow-motion replay, arrows ask 'who pushed?' and fade to nothing.

lines.text: The answer hides in three rules from Sir Isaac Newton.
lines.visual: Whip-pan to a navy night sky. Three glowing cards (blue, orange, green) pop in with an apple that wobbles.

lines.text: Let's master them with autos, cricket balls and an ISRO rocket!
lines.visual: Auto-rickshaw, cricket ball and rocket zoom across the screen, title 'Newton's Three Laws' slams in with screen shake.

lines.text: Law number one. The law of inertia.
lines.visual: Blue shape-wipe transition. Chapter tag 'LAW 1' appears top-left. Title with bounce.

lines.text: An object stays at rest, or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
lines.visual: Kinetic typography: key words (rest, straight line, constant speed, unbalanced force) pop in time with the voice and glow blue.

lines.text: Balanced forces cancel, like a tug of war between equal teams. Unbalanced forces change the motion.
lines.visual: Tug of war: two equal force arrows (50 N each) keep the knot still. Then one arrow grows to 80 N, arrow turns red and the knot slides.

lines.text: Back to the bus. Your body was moving with it. The bus stops, but your body keeps going. So you lurch forward!
lines.visual: Split replay of the bus. Dotted line shows the bus stopping while Newt's path continues. Speed lines, dust puff, screen shake.

lines.text: That is inertia: the tendency to resist any change in motion.
lines.visual: The word INERTIA is built letter by letter with overshoot.

lines.text: Inertia of rest. Yank a tablecloth fast and the plates stay put. Flick the card and the coin drops into the glass. Beat a dusty carpet and the dust falls out.
lines.visual: Three mini-demos in a row, each dimmed until its sentence: tablecloth trick, coin on a card dropping into a glass, carpet beating with dust puffs.

lines.text: Inertia of motion. A runner keeps running a few steps after the finish line.
lines.visual: Runner crosses the finish tape, slides forward with squash and stretch, motion blur.

lines.text: Inertia of direction. When an auto turns left, you slide right.
lines.visual: Top-down view of an auto taking a left turn, passenger dot continues straight along a dotted arrow.

lines.text: Heavier objects have more inertia. Mass measures inertia.
lines.visual: Split screen: light football vs heavy iron ball, same push; heavy one barely moves. Label 'More mass = more inertia'.

lines.text: That is why seatbelts matter. In a crash the car stops, but you don't. The belt stops you safely.
lines.visual: Slow-motion crash freeze frame with callout labels 'Car stops' and 'Body keeps moving'; seatbelt snaps across Newt and a green tick pops.

lines.text: Which is harder to push: an empty cart, or a cart full of vegetables?
lines.visual: Orange wipe. Chapter tag 'LAW 2'. Split screen: Newt pushes an empty cart (fast, light) vs a full vegetable cart (slow, heavy). Wind-up anticipation before each push.

lines.text: The full one! Now give a cricket ball and a football the same kick. The lighter cricket ball speeds up more.
lines.visual: Same-size force arrow (40 N) on both. Cricket ball (0.16 kg) flies in a big arc, football (0.43 kg) in a lower arc. Arrows and numbers labelled.

lines.text: Law number two. Acceleration is directly proportional to the net force, and inversely proportional to the mass.
lines.visual: Kinetic typography in orange. The words 'directly' and 'inversely' flip with a small bounce.

lines.text: Together, that is F equals m times a.
lines.visual: The equation assembles piece by piece: F slides in from left, = drops from top, m pops, x spins in, a zooms in. Pieces glow in turn.

lines.text: F is force in newtons. m is mass in kilograms. a is acceleration in metres per second squared.
lines.visual: Each letter gets a unit tag: N, kg, m/s². Tags land with a pop.

lines.text: Momentum is mass times velocity. Force is how fast momentum changes. For constant mass, that is F equals m times a.
lines.visual: Equation morphs: p = m v, then F = change in p / change in t, then F = m a. Match-cut back to the main formula.

lines.text: Double the force, double the acceleration. Double the mass, half the acceleration.
lines.visual: Live bar graph: force bar doubles, acceleration bar doubles; mass doubles, acceleration bar halves.

lines.text: Numerical time! An auto-rickshaw of five hundred kilograms gets a net force of one thousand newtons. Find its acceleration, and its speed after five seconds from rest.
lines.visual: Chalkboard card slides in with the question. Auto-rickshaw sits at the start line.

lines.text: Given: m is five hundred kilograms, F is one thousand newtons, u is zero.
lines.visual: 'Given' list types in with units; each value highlights as spoken.

lines.text: a equals F divided by m, so a equals one thousand divided by five hundred, which is two metres per second squared.
lines.visual: Numbers drop in, counter animates 1000 / 500 = 2 m/s². Auto accelerates slowly with speed lines.

lines.text: Then v equals u plus a times t, which is zero plus two times five, so ten metres per second.
lines.visual: Live speedometer and velocity-time graph draw a straight line up to 10 m/s at t = 5 s.

lines.text: That is thirty six kilometres per hour!
lines.visual: Speedometer needle overshoots and settles at 36 km/h; confetti sparks. Newt cheers.

lines.text: Law number three! Action and reaction.
lines.visual: Green wipe. Chapter tag 'LAW 3'. Two hands push each other and spring apart.

lines.text: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
lines.visual: Kinetic typography; 'equal' and 'opposite' appear as two arrows pointing apart.

lines.text: If A pushes B, then B pushes A back, equally hard, in the opposite direction.
lines.visual: Two skaters push off each other; arrows of equal length (60 N each) in opposite directions, skaters slide apart (lighter one faster).

lines.text: An ISRO rocket pushes hot gases down, and the gases push the rocket up.
lines.visual: Rocket on pad, anticipation shake, countdown, lift-off with flame particles; gas arrow down, thrust arrow up; screen shake.

lines.text: A swimmer pushes water back, and the water pushes the swimmer forward.
lines.visual: Side view of a swimmer in a pool, water arrows backward and forward.

lines.text: A gun pushes the bullet forward, and the bullet kicks the gun back. That is recoil.
lines.visual: Toy cannon on a cart fires a ball; cannon rolls back with a puff of smoke. Labels 'Action' and 'Reaction'.

lines.text: When you walk, your foot pushes the ground back, and the ground pushes you forward.
lines.visual: Foot-level view; arrow on ground and arrow on foot; Newt slips on a banana peel with squash and stretch.

lines.text: A released balloon: air rushes out, and the balloon zooms the other way!
lines.visual: Balloon released, flies around in a loopy arc with a wobbling tail.

lines.text: But if the forces are equal and opposite, why don't they cancel?
lines.visual: Freeze frame, question marks orbit Newt's head.

lines.text: Because they act on different objects! Action on the ball, reaction on your foot. Forces cancel only on the same object.
lines.visual: Foot and ball, two coloured arrows each with a halo around its own object; a dotted line shows 'cancel' only works inside one halo.

lines.text: Recap! Law one: objects resist changes in motion.
lines.visual: Three cards fly in, blue card flips up first with an inertia icon.

lines.text: Law two: force equals mass times acceleration.
lines.visual: Orange card flips, F = m a pulses.

lines.text: Law three: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
lines.visual: Green card flips, two arrows bounce apart.

lines.text: Quick quiz! Three questions, five seconds each.
lines.visual: Newt in a game-show pose, 'QUIZ TIME' banner with confetti.

lines.text: Question one. A bus stops and you lurch forward. A, law one? B, law two? C, law three?
lines.visual: Options A, B, C slide in; 5 second ring countdown timer.

lines.text: A! Law one.
lines.visual: Wrong options fade, A grows green with a tick; Newt jumps.

lines.text: Question two. Twenty newtons acts on a four kilogram trolley. What is its acceleration in metres per second squared? A, two. B, five. C, eighty.
lines.visual: Trolley, options A, B, C, 5 second countdown.

lines.text: B! Twenty divided by four is five.
lines.visual: B glows; a = 20 / 4 = 5 m/s² counts up.

lines.text: Question three. A rocket rises because gases are pushed down. A, law one? B, law two? C, law three?
lines.visual: Rocket icon, options A, B, C, 5 second countdown.

lines.text: C! Action and reaction.
lines.visual: C glows green; rocket lifts off.

lines.text: You nailed it! Go spot Newton's laws everywhere. See you next time!
lines.visual: Newt waves, three cards orbit, end card with fade-out.
